children: Tokenization infrastructure firm Fission has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Pantera Capital. It wants to make it easier for eligible investors to sell tokenized private-market holdings without waiting for traditional fund redemption periods.
The tokenization industry has spent years promising faster transfers of financial assets. Fission now wants to solve a more difficult problem: what happens when an investor wants their money back?
The financial technology company announced on October 15 that it had raised $10 million in a round led by Pantera Capital, with participation from Circle Ventures and other investors.
Its business focuses on liquidity for tokenized alternative investments, including private funds that are traditionally difficult to sell quickly.
A Token Is Not The Same As A Buyer
Representing ownership of a fund on a blockchain may make recordkeeping and transfers more efficient. It does not automatically create a liquid market.
A private credit or private equity fund can still have transfer restrictions, limited redemption windows and few willing buyers.

Fission is developing infrastructure to provide secondary-market liquidity for qualifying interests. Some transactions can be completed rapidly when liquidity is available, but that should not be confused with a guaranteed right to sell every asset instantly at full value.
The company’s approach complements the industry’s wider interest in tokenized institutional investment products.
Investors increasingly want to know how tokenized assets can be financed, transferred and redeemed, not simply how they are issued.
Fission plans to use the money to extend its infrastructure and support more asset managers.
Pantera’s investment suggests that solving practical market problems may be at least as commercially significant as launching another blockchain-based security.
Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Pantera Leads $10 Million Fission Funding Round To Solve Tokenized Fund Liquidity Problem
